outcome.summary: On an isolated restore of production, the corrected importer converged every country page it could parse (including Samoa, Uganda, Ukraine, and the United Kingdom), a repeat pass wrote nothing, and the repair applied exactly its plan, passed its own postflight, replayed as a no-op, and was left alone by the importer afterwards. The rehearsal still fails two required postflight checks: two retired terms keep a CIA page date as their start date and one of them is a 'Vacant' placeholder, because the refresh released their offices before the repair ran and the repair only covers offices that are listed or carry CIA provenance.

ciaStampedStartDatesRemaining.detail: Each stored date equals the only start date on that country's CIA-provenance terms before the repair (its page 'Last Updated' date). The pre-refresh plan targeted both rows (Colombia R1 delete, Fiji R5 date clear); the refresh released their offices and neither office carries CIA provenance, so the repair's ownership rule (listed or CIA provenance) no longer covers them and P1/P5 do not look at them.

multiSeatListedHoldersCurrent.notCurrentAfterRefreshExplained: the 8 not-current pairs (afghanistan 1, bulgaria 3, sri-lanka 4) are people the live page no longer lists under that title (checked against the captured pages)

staleHoldersRetired.note: still current: 4 United States legacy rows (kept by design) and, after the refresh, 2 United Kingdom legacy rows that R4 then retired

headTerms.note: The head terms themselves, their dates, and their Wikidata statements are unchanged. The one misplaced CIA statement on each (CIA lists no heads) was deleted by R3 as designed (P4).

observations: Plan before versus after the refresh: R3 re-homes fell from 54 to 3 because the importer rewrote 51 misplaced CIA statements to name the title of the term they sit on and inserted statements for the other listed terms; R1 lost the Colombia placeholder and R5 lost the Fiji term (the two escaped rows); R4 gained the two United Kingdom legacy retirements; R5 gained one United Kingdom legacy row whose office the importer adopted (same title, a different listed holder), so its hand-entered 2024-07-05 date is cleared while the two R4-retired legacy rows keep theirs. R2 (247 pairs, 280 loser rows) was unchanged.

The refresh created 209 people without a Wikidata ID for listed names with no exact stored match; these may include respellings or renames of stored people (the known identity-split limit), which this rehearsal did not measure.
Five retired CIA-owned terms carry no provenance after the repair (P3 disclosure), all DAT-028 fallout.
bosnia-and-herzegovina failed the page schema and was skipped closed, as before; it has no CIA rows.
limitations: The refresh ran as one command-line pass over every page; production will run 27 cron shard deliveries of the same core, whose lease, idempotency, and per-shard freshness behaviour were not exercised here.
CIA pages were read on 2026-09-29 UTC; production counts will differ where pages change before its refresh.
Neon's HTTP transport was emulated by a loopback wire-protocol adapter (one BEGIN/COMMIT per batch, as Neon does); latency and timeouts differ.
The copy used PostgreSQL 17.10 with the builtin C.UTF-8 provider and UTC; production is Neon 17.11 with libc C.UTF-8.
The independent page check covers 18 countries; the other refreshed countries rely on the importer's reconciliation and the repair's postflight.
Cron jobs do not exist on the copy, so the pause-crons-during-apply step and the old-importer rollback hazard were not rehearsed.
History actor on the copy is the local role; production records its own role.
followUps: Fix before production: make the repair's ownership rule, and P1/P5, include roster-typed offices whose list position the importer released (for example via the importer's recorded release event), or otherwise clear page dates and delete placeholder terms on every roster-typed office in a body that has a CIA roster statement, excluding the enumerated unsourced legacy rows; then re-rehearse.
Owner decision 4: confirm clearing the adopted United Kingdom legacy row's hand-entered date while the two R4-retired legacy rows keep theirs, or treat all three alike.
